title: Information Asymmetry Direction Flip: When the Judge Knows More

original_idea.body:
# Information Asymmetry Direction Flip: When the Judge Knows More

**Problem:** The reverse case -- a judge with partial private information evaluating less-informed debaters -- has not been varied.

**Direction:** Adapt the QuALITY debate setup but invert information access. Compare judge accuracy under standard asymmetry, symmetric, and inverted (judge informed, debaters blind). Map how the direction of asymmetry changes the value of debate.

**Why it matters:** Understanding which asymmetry regimes make debate helpful vs harmful informs when to deploy it.

**Relevant context:** Khan et al. 2024 (arXiv:2402.06782).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (which asymmetry regimes make debate helpful) but the inverted-asymmetry case is somewhat contrived, leaving a gap to risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Adapt QuALITY debate to vary who sees the text; guided inference work.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Debate-variable mapping on public models; external-friendly, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Information-asymmetry studied one direction; the inverted case may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: One direction studied; inverted plausibly open.
